title: Accurate structural modelling of protein-glycan recognition with GlycoWeave
summary: Protein-glycan recognition underlies diverse biological processes, yet accurate prediction of protein-glycan complex structures remains challenging owing to the chemical diversity, conformational flexibility and sparse experimental structural coverage of glycans. Here we present GlycoWeave, a glycan-specific diffusion framework that integrates chemically constrained conformational sampling, multiscale molecular representations and multi-source learning. By operating in internal-coordinate space, GlycoWeave preserves glycan connectivity and stereochemistry while efficiently exploring bound conformations. A heterogeneous equivariant network couples atom-level interaction geometry with monosaccharide-level structural context, whereas multi-source, multi-head training integrates experimental complexes with structures refined using classical and quantum mechanics-informed potentials. On a benchmark of 698 protein-glycan complexes, GlycoWeave achieves a 71.9% Top-25 high-quality success rate, compared with 19.2% for AlphaFold 3, while requiring only 0.34 s per sampled pose. GlycoWeave further preserves glycan structural validity, recovers native protein-glycan interactions and reproduces linkage-specific conformational preferences, maintaining high accuracy across diverse glycan architectures and protein environments. These results establish GlycoWeave as an accurate, efficient and chemically faithful framework for modelling protein-glycan recognition. GlycoWeave is freely available at https://cadd.zju.edu.cn/glycoweave.

AI.tldr: GlycoWeave是一种专用于预测蛋白质-糖复合物结构的扩散框架，通过整合化学约束的构象采样和多源学习，显著提高了预测精度和效率。
AI.motivation: 蛋白质-糖识别影响多种生物过程，但由于糖的化学多样性、构象灵活性及实验结构覆盖不足，准确预测其复合物结构具有挑战性。
AI.method: GlycoWeave采用内部坐标空间操作，结合异构等变网络和多源训练，整合实验和计算结构数据。
AI.result: 在698个复合物的基准测试中，GlycoWeave的高质量预测成功率达到71.9%，远超AlphaFold 3的19.2%，且每采样姿态仅需0.34秒。
AI.conclusion: GlycoWeave是一种准确、高效且化学可靠的蛋白质-糖识别建模工具。

title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
summary: The behavior of biomolecular complexes is governed by chemically specific interactions and often involves rare events that atomistic molecular dynamics struggle to capture within accessible timescales. Here we introduce AMARO v2.0, a coarse-grained neural network potential that retains all heavy atoms and treats solvent implicitly. Hydrogen-aware bead types and total-charge conditioning provide a shared representation for proteins, drug-like molecules, and their complexes, including ternary protein-protein-ligand systems. The model preserves folded proteins and captures key features of protein conformational free-energy landscapes. Across 262 complexes spanning 11 targets, the learned potential retains most ligand poses, although quaternary structure reorientation is observed for the HIF2A ternary complex. In targeted case studies, AMARO v2.0 distinguishes the two protonation states of trypsin-benzamidine and reaches the crystal binding pose in 3.3-fold more trajectories than all-atom molecular mechanics at a fixed estimated GPU-time budget. The same framework also recovers a reference binding pose in TYK2 and supports binding free-energy estimation for both trypsin-benzamidine and TYK2-EJM31, although the resulting values are more energetically favorable than the experimental references. SHP2 and CDK8 systems expose remaining limitations in binding-pose recovery and site specificity, respectively. Together, these results support AMARO v2.0 as a shared heavy-atom potential for biomolecular complex dynamics.

AI.tldr: AMARO v2.0是一种保留所有重原子并隐式处理溶剂的粗粒度神经网络势能模型，适用于蛋白质、药物样分子及其复合物的动力学模拟，包括三元蛋白-蛋白-配体系统。
AI.motivation: 原子分子动力学难以在可达到的时间尺度内捕捉生物分子复合物的罕见事件，因此需要一种更具效率的粗粒度模型。
AI.method: AMARO v2.0采用氢感知的珠子类型和总电荷条件，提供共享表示，并在多个复合物系统中测试。
AI.result: 模型保留了折叠蛋白质，并捕获了蛋白质构象自由能景观；在262个复合物中，大多数配体构象得以保留，但在HIF2A三元复合物中观察到四级结构重新定向。在某些案例中，模型性能优于全原子分子力学。
AI.conclusion: AMARO v2.0是一种有效的共享重原子势能模型，可用于生物分子复合物动力学研究，但仍存在某些局限性。
